groups.problem: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens.
groups.rationale: Both report the same wrong third argument at the same call site in zoho-bigin CalendarService.

groups.problem: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect provider-specific shapes (.data, HubspotToken, etc.).
groups.rationale: All describe the same inconsistent return contract of refreshOAuthTokens; normalizing its return shape fixes every caller.

groups.problem: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()] that produce literal keys instead of a catchall, so expiry and other fields are not validated or are stripped.
groups.rationale: All three point at the same flawed computed-key schema and suggest passthrough/catchall/record.

groups.problem: encodeOAuthState just echoes req.query.state like decodeOAuthState instead of building and encoding the OAuth state (teamId, returnTo).
groups.rationale: All report that the new encodeOAuthState is a copy of decode and no longer encodes state.

groups.problem: Google CalendarService stores the SafeParse result wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key instead of its .data.
groups.rationale: Same line, same problem: the wrapper object is persisted as the credential key.

groups.problem: decodeOAuthState calls JSON.parse on req.query.state without try/catch, so malformed state causes a 500.
groups.rationale: Both report the same unguarded JSON.parse in decodeOAuthState.

problems: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens.
On the sync path, Bigin expects an Axios response with .data but receives a fetch Response.
The webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a timing-safe comparison.
The header name lookup is case-sensitive.
There is no HTTP method check, so GET requests can write credentials.
uncoveredProblems: The webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a timing-safe comparison.
The header name from the env var is not lowercased, so the lookup can fail.
The webhook handler does not enforce POST, so any method can write credentials.

problems: Decrypt and JSON.parse of the webhook keys have no try/catch, so failures return a 500.
The encryption key falls back to an empty string and its length is not validated.
uncoveredProblems: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse in the webhook are not wrapped in error handling.
The encryption key falls back to an empty string and its length is not validated.

problems: Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma without importing it.
uncoveredProblems: Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma.credential.update without importing prisma.
Salesforce token refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens and credential sync.
Checking response.statusText !== 'OK' is an unreliable success check.
